structured_output.summary: The draft covers B12's scope and done_when and nothing more. It is opt-in per track (Dust Bowl only), keeps bot laps and replays unchanged (AI never collects, and collecting alone never changes car state), and follows UI_RULES §6 and the mockups for the ⌀64 action button above GAS and the SPACE · POWER-UP keycap. Each criterion tests one observable behaviour through a public seam. The remaining issues are minor and go to the builder.

findings.claim: The draft never says what a pickup box looks like. A plain mustard box shaded per §8 (top mustard, sides dirt) looks just like a hay bale (render/props.ts: mustard box, 1.2 tall, the size of the sim's collider). Hay bales are obstacles, so a player could steer around pickups thinking they are bales.
findings.suggestedFix: Builder: build the pickup only from what §8 already allows: palette-index mustard top, dirt sides, ink inverted-hull outline, flat ink blob shadow. Make it a single cube clearly smaller than a bale (about 1 unit) and place it alone on the dirt ribbon, never in a row beside the track, so where it sits is what tells it apart. No new colours, glow, spin or bob animation (§7 bans idle pulsing).

findings.claim: The action button's states need pinning. The S1–S2 mockup shows it unarmed as a dirt roundel with a dark-dirt lightning glyph, but §10's generic disabled state is dark-dirt with no shadow, and §6 uses mustard for pressed touch controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Builder: unarmed follows the S1–S2 mockup (dirt fill, dark-dirt glyph, ink ring). Armed fill is mustard (§1: mustard = pickups) with an ink glyph. Keep the §6 resting/active behaviour shared with the other controls. Use the existing wake pop (0.9→1 scale, transform only, motion tokens) as the collect pop, cut under reduced motion. Colours cut, never tween.

findings.claim: Existing tests/ui/touch-state.test.ts maps TOUCH_CONTROL_IDS and expects exactly 4 states, 4 .ui-tc buttons and 4 zones from a plain createTouchControls(). Adding 'action' to TOUCH_CONTROL_IDS, or always rendering the button, would break append-only tests.
findings.suggestedFix: Builder: leave TOUCH_CONTROL_IDS and the default createTouchControls() output unchanged. Add the action button and its zone only when the race UI turns it on (a RaceView whose player racer has `armed`), as AC8 already says.

findings.claim: AC4 says 'at 25 units/s', but dirt topSpeed is 25 and acceleration tapers as (1−u²), so the car only approaches 25 and never reaches it exactly. AC4 also needs about 3.5 s of mostly-dirt driving to watch the boost and the decay (overSpeedDrag 2.2 takes 32 down to about 25.1 within 120 ticks, so the 25.5 bound holds).
findings.suggestedFix: Builder: write the AC4 test as 'speed ≥ 24 before firing', and steer car 0 with the bot's steer (throttle held) so it stays on dirt. Assert the max-speed bound of 32 on every tick of the boost.

findings.claim: AC8's 'marked popping' doesn't say what can be observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Builder: make the pop observable the way the existing wake pop is: a state class added on the sync where armed turns true and removed after the motion duration. Test that it appears on that sync and not on later syncs while armed stays true.

findings.claim: src/ui/keycap-legend.ts's header comment says there is no power-up binding and so no SPACE key. That becomes stale. src/sim/replay.ts also describes bit2 as 'reserved'.
findings.suggestedFix: Builder: update both comments to describe the new behaviour: SPACE · POWER-UP only on pickup tracks, and bit2 = action.

findings.claim: Play-test step 2 needs a full 3-lap Bramble Bends race before Dust Bowl can be reached, because track select (B08, #30) isn't merged. That works but is slow on a phone.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the step, but mention in the run notes that the owner can retire from Bramble Bends faster by finishing quickly. Nothing in the spec changes.

structured_output.overlapAssessment: The harness reports no file overlap. #30 (B08), #31 (B09) and #32 (maintenance) list zero files, and the only diff in /inputs is #29. #29 adds the hay-loop bot-lap baseline and a best-lap browser test. That test drives Dust Bowl with bot inputs. It never fires action, collecting changes no car state, and the action button sits bottom-right, away from the NEW BEST chip, so #29 still passes. B09 (#31) may change touch-controls and race-ui to slide touch slots in. B12 doesn't build on it. At worst both edit those files, a mechanical rebase, and the new action slot would need adding to B09's slide-in afterwards. That doesn't change either feature, so building tonight is safe.
